paperMetadata.title: Scaling Multimodal Large Language Models with Transformers

abstract: We propose a novel architecture called UniModalTransformer (UMT), designed to enhance the integration of multimodal data across visual, textual, and auditory modalities. Our approach addresses the challenge of cross-modal alignment by employing a unified transformer architecture that processes these diverse data types concurrently. Unlike existing models that often treat modalities in isolation or rely on late fusion techniques, UMT introduces an interleaved attention mechanism that facilitates early fusion and shared representation learning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of UMT through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in visual reasoning and audio-visual tasks. Our contributions also include a new dataset for cross-modal instruction tuning and a comprehensive analysis of model scalability across different modality combinations.

contributions.title: Unified Transformer Architecture for Multimodal Data
contributions.description: We introduce a novel transformer-based architecture that integrates visual, textual, and auditory data through a shared transformer backbone, enabling concurrent processing and interaction between modalities.
contributions.novelty: This approach facilitates early fusion and joint representation learning, contrasting with existing models that often rely on separate processing pipelines or late fusion techniques.

contributions.title: Interleaved Attention Mechanism
contributions.description: Our model employs an interleaved attention mechanism that allows for dynamic cross-modal interactions by adjusting attention weights based on the contextual relevance of each modality.
contributions.novelty: This mechanism enhances the model's ability to align and integrate multimodal information, improving performance in tasks requiring cross-modal reasoning.

contributions.title: Cross-Modal Instruction Tuning Dataset
contributions.description: We release a new dataset designed to facilitate instruction tuning across multiple modalities, providing diverse tasks that require integrated visual, textual, and auditory understanding.
contributions.novelty: This dataset fills a gap in existing resources by offering complex, multimodal instructions that demand concurrent reasoning across different data types.

methodology.problemFormulation: The problem involves developing a scalable model capable of integrating and processing multimodal data to improve cross-modal understanding and reasoning.
methodology.approach: Our approach leverages a transformer architecture with shared weights across modalities, combined with an interleaved attention mechanism to dynamically prioritize relevant modal interactions.

components.name: Unified Transformer Backbone
components.role: Processes all input modalities through a shared architecture, enabling unified representation learning.
components.details: The backbone consists of multiple transformer layers that share parameters across modalities, allowing for efficient scaling and parameter sharing.

components.name: Interleaved Attention Module
components.role: Facilitates cross-modal interaction by dynamically adjusting attention weights based on contextual relevance.
components.details: This module computes attention scores by considering the interactions between modalities at each layer, enhancing cross-modal understanding.

assumptions: Input modalities are synchronized and pre-processed to a compatible format.
Sufficient computational resources are available to train large-scale transformer models.
limitations: The model may require significant computational resources for training and inference.
Performance may degrade if input modalities are not well-aligned or pre-processed adequately.

Further research will investigate advanced techniques for better aligning modalities to improve model performance, especially in noisy data conditions.
